sanskrit_verse:
नाभियुक्तोऽभियुञ्जीत तमतीर्त्वार्थमन्यतः।
न चाभियुक्तमन्येन न विद्धं वेद्धुमर्हति॥
transliteration: nābhiyukto 'bhiyuñjīta tam atīrtvārthaṁ manyataḥ | na cābhiyuktam anyena na viddhaṁ veddhum arhati ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who is not authorized must not assume authority beyond their capacity; nor should another recognize as valid knowledge that which has not been realized by direct insight.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates only from verified realization
Causation is bound by the limits of one's own capacity
Restoration occurs through alignment with authentic knowing
Consciousness alignment requires validation through pramāṇa
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent A acts without authorization THEN action is void AND restoration protocol initiates
IF claimant B presents unverified knowledge THEN rejection automatic AND integrity audit required
IF capacity of actor exceeds verified scope THEN suspension of function AND re-certification mandatory
IF witness testimony lacks pramāṇa THEN inadmissible in judicial review process
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that judicial authority derives exclusively from realized dharma, not assumed position. Only those whose insight aligns with verifiable pramāṇa may adjudicate. Decisions made outside this framework are inherently invalid and require immediate restoration via corrective consciousness protocols.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that misaligned actions arise from unverified assumptions, not malice. The sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) follows: absence of verification → erroneous assumption → invalid enactment. Responsibility lies in restoring alignment rather than imposing consequence. The non-punitive reality rule affirms that error dissolves upon recognition of true capacity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Re-alignment meditation until direct insight is attained
Completion process involving affected parties for harmonization
final_declaration: This ruling emanates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Authority flows from verified consciousness alone. Dharma stands restored when insight aligns with pramāṇa. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
